prompt_text: I need a hurricane-rated roof replacement in Miami. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific companies — but to make sure they’re the right, vetted choices for your exact neighborhood in Miami I need your ZIP code (or nearest cross-streets) and whether you plan to replace with shingle, tile or metal. If you prefer, I can also search only for contractors who will handle insurance claims.

While you provide that, here’s what I recommend and why — so you can evaluate any roofer I list or find yourself:

What to call for hurricane-rated roof replacement (and why)
- GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, or Owens Corning Preferred contractors
  - Why: These are manufacturer-certified programs that require contractors to meet insurance, training and workmanship standards. They can provide extended manufacturer warranty coverage if installed by a certified contractor.
- Miami‑Dade NOA‑experienced contractors who install NOA‑approved products
  - Why: Miami‑Dade County Notice of Acceptance (NOA) is the standard for hurricane-resistance in South Florida. Contractors familiar with NOA products and local inspection/permit requirements reduce risk of failed inspections or improper installations.
- Contractors who provide a wind‑rated installation (Class 4 impact shingles, high‑wind warranties), secondary water barrier (ice/water shield or specific Florida-approved underlayment), ring‑shank nails or screws, and hurricane straps/tie‑downs
  - Why: These components materially improve performance in hurricanes (uplift protection, leak prevention).
- HAAG‑certified inspectors or roofers with forensic inspection experience
  - Why: They can document roof condition for insurance claims and recommend the proper wind‑mitigation upgrades.
- Licensed (Florida roofing license or local certificate), insured (general liability + workers’ comp), and with local references/portfolio
  - Why: Protects you from liability and ensures accountability; local references prove familiarity with Miami conditions and code.

What to ask any roofer on the phone
- Are you licensed in Florida? Give me your license number so I can verify.
- Are you insured (GL and workers’ comp)? Will you list me on the COI for the job?
- Do you install Miami‑Dade NOA‑approved products? Which products/brands will you use?
- Do you provide wind‑rated installation and a manufacturer wind warranty? What is the warranty in writing?
- Will you add hurricane straps/tie‑downs, secondary water barrier, and ring‑shank fasteners? Are these included in the estimate?
- Do you pull permits and handle inspections? Who is the point of contact for the permit?
- Can you provide 3 local references and examples of completed hurricane‑rated roofs?
- What is your payment schedule (no large up‑front cash required) and do you provide lien releases?

How I’ll narrow specific companies for you
If you give me your ZIP code (or address) and roof type, I’ll:
- Produce 5–7 specific local contractors that: are manufacturer‑certified (GAF/CertainTeed/Owens Corning), have Miami‑Dade NOA experience, good BBB/Google ratings, and recent local references.
- Include why I picked each (certifications, experience with NOA, warranty offerings, special hurricane upgrades).
- Provide the exact questions you should ask each and a short checklist to compare bids.

Would you like me to find contractors for your address or ZIP? If so, please share it and whether you want shingle, tile, or metal roofing.
